# ol-prefix

- ID: `MD029`
- Category: Lists
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `ol`

Ordered list items are numbered 1, 1, 1, or 1, 2, 3, or 0, 1, 2, and so on.

## Why

Renderers number the items themselves and use only the first number, so other
numbers in the source can disagree with the output.

## Options

Set them under `rules.ol-prefix.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `one_or_ordered`): Numbering to require: all ones,
  increasing numbers, all zeros, or one\_or\_ordered, which accepts either of
  the first two. Values: `one`, `ordered`, `one_or_ordered`, `zero`.
- `allow_renumbering` (`boolean`, default `true`, gomdlint only): Fix a wrong
  number. With false, wrong numbers are reported without a fix.

## Fix

The fix renumbers the items. gomdlint reports a list without a fix when
renumbering it would change its first number, which sets where the rendered list
starts. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would change a
line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around
it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list checkbox. In a
document with raw HTML other than comments and plain br, wbr, hr or img tags,
gomdlint reports every finding without a fix.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  ol-prefix:
    options:
      style: one_or_ordered
```

Under `rules`, `ol-prefix: false` turns the rule off and `ol-prefix: error`
reports its findings as errors. The flag `--disable ol-prefix` turns it off for
one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line ol-prefix -->
```
